lead: A centrifugal pump can spin without lifting water. It starts delivering only when the head created by its impeller at shut-off reaches the manometric head. That speed is the minimum starting speed. Designers also combine pumps: in series to add head, in parallel to add flow. The reasoning is like pipes in series and parallel, but now the curves belong to pumps. Borewell booster sets, multi-stage water supply pumps and fire-fighting headers use these ideas.
prereq: You need: heads and manometric efficiency from 7.3, and the idea of pipes in series and parallel from Unit 4.

blocks.text: At standstill the impeller cannot push water into a delivery pipe that already needs a pressure head. The pressure head the pump must produce is the manometric head H<sub>m</sub>. With the delivery valve closed, flow Q is zero; this is shut-off. The impeller still creates a head because it spins the water. At the outlet the peripheral velocity is u = πDN/60, where u is in m/s, D is the impeller outlet diameter in m and N is the speed in rpm.

For the ideal shut-off model, the head imparted by the impeller is H<sub>e</sub> = u²/g. Manometric efficiency is η<sub>man</sub> = H<sub>m</sub>/H<sub>e</sub>, so H<sub>e</sub> = H<sub>m</sub>/η<sub>man</sub>. Put the two expressions for H<sub>e</sub> equal and solve for N.

blocks.where: N<sub>min</sub> is the minimum starting speed in rpm; D is the impeller outlet diameter in m; H<sub>m</sub> is the manometric head in m; g = 9.81 m/s²; η<sub>man</sub> is the manometric efficiency, dimensionless. Use η<sub>man</sub> = 1 if efficiency is not used.

blocks.text: Below N<sub>min</sub> the impeller head is less than H<sub>m</sub>, so the pump cannot deliver water. At N<sub>min</sub> it just starts delivering. Real pumps need a little more speed to cover losses and clearance. This estimate is used while selecting a motor for a pump that must start against a closed delivery valve.

In series, the delivery of pump 1 is connected to the suction of pump 2. The same discharge Q passes through both pumps. Each pump adds head at that Q. The total head is H = H<sub>1</sub> + H<sub>2</sub> at the same Q.

For two identical pumps, H = 2H<sub>1</sub>(Q). This is how a multi-stage pump works: each stage adds head while the flow stays the same. Use series when the system needs high head and the flow is low, such as lifting water from a deep borewell or feeding a boiler.
The second pump and its casing must withstand the higher pressure produced by the first pump. Series connection does not add flows. Do not add Q<sub>1</sub> + Q<sub>2</sub> here; the flow is common.

In parallel, both pumps draw from a common suction header and deliver into a common delivery header. The head H is the same across each pump. The flows add: Q = Q<sub>1</sub> + Q<sub>2</sub> at the same H. For identical pumps, Q = 2Q<sub>1</sub>(H). Use parallel operation for high flow at moderate head, such as a city water booster or a fire-fighting header.
The figure uses two identical pumps. At Q = 40 L/s one pump gives 30 m. Two in series give 60 m at the same Q. Two in parallel give 35 m at total Q = 40 L/s, because each pump passes 20 L/s.
Do not add both head and flow. In series Q is the same; in parallel H is the same. For unequal pumps, the split follows the common head. Full characteristic curves and the duty point are in 7.6.

figure.caption: At the same flow the series line is twice the single-pump head; the parallel line gives the same head at twice the flow. The example values at Q = 40 L/s are 60 m in series, 30 m for one pump and 35 m in parallel.

spec.aria: Three lines show one pump, two pumps in series with double head at the same flow, and two pumps in parallel with double flow at the same head.

examples.question: A centrifugal pump has the characteristic H = 40 − 0.25Q, with H in m and Q in L/s. Two identical pumps are connected in series and in parallel. Find the head at Q = 40 L/s for one pump, two pumps in series, and two pumps in parallel.
steps: Two pumps in series carry the same Q = 40 L/s. Each pump develops 30 m, so H<sub>series</sub> = 30 + 30 = 60 m. Using the series curve: H = 80 − 0.5 × 40 = 80 − 20 = 60 m.

Two pumps in parallel have the same head. The total Q = 40 L/s splits equally between identical pumps, so each pump passes Q<sub>each</sub> = 20 L/s. Each head is H = 40 − 0.25 × 20 = 40 − 5 = 35 m. Using the parallel curve: H = 40 − 0.125 × 40 = 40 − 5 = 35 m.
examples.answer: At Q = 40 L/s the head is 30 m for one pump, 60 m for two pumps in series and 35 m for two pumps in parallel.
examples.check:
Q = 40.0
H_one = 40 - 0.25*Q
H_series = 2*H_one
Q_each = Q/2
H_parallel = 40 - 0.25*Q_each
print(round(H_one, 1))
print(round(H_series, 1))
print(round(H_parallel, 1))

traps: In series the flow is the same and heads add; in parallel the head is the same and flows add. Do not add both head and flow.
The minimum-speed formula uses D in metres and N in rpm. Using D in mm, or using angular speed in rad/s, gives a wrong answer. Convert η<sub>man</sub> from percent to decimal.
At Q = 0 the pump still has shut-off head. Zero flow does not mean zero head. Minimum starting speed is where impeller head equals manometric head.
For identical pumps in parallel at total Q, each pump takes Q/2 only when the curves are identical. Unequal pumps split according to the common head.
Series pumps do not double flow; parallel pumps do not double head. The examiner's favourite question asks for both at one Q.

quiz.q: Define minimum starting speed of a centrifugal pump.
quiz.a: The lowest speed at which the impeller head at shut-off equals the manometric head, so the pump just starts delivering water.

quiz.q: Write the formula for N<sub>min</sub> and state what D and H<sub>m</sub> mean.
quiz.a: N<sub>min</sub> = (60/(πD))√(gH<sub>m</sub>/η<sub>man</sub>). D is impeller outlet diameter in m; H<sub>m</sub> is manometric head in m.

quiz.q: Why does a pump not deliver water below N<sub>min</sub>?
quiz.a: The impeller head is below the manometric head, so it cannot overcome the delivery pressure and water does not rise.

quiz.q: A pump has D = 0.25 m, H<sub>m</sub> = 20 m and η<sub>man</sub> = 0.8. Find N<sub>min</sub>.
Two identical pumps in parallel each follow H = 40 − 0.25Q, with Q per pump in L/s. Find the head when total Q = 60 L/s.
quiz.a: Each pump passes 30 L/s, so H = 40 − 0.25 × 30 = 32.5 m.

quiz.q: Why does a series connection not simply double the flow in a pipe system?
quiz.a: Series doubles head at a given Q. The operating point moves along the system curve to a higher Q, but system friction rises with Q², so flow increases by less than double.

quiz.q: Why are check valves fitted when pumps run in parallel?
quiz.a: If one pump stops, its check valve closes and prevents backflow through it; the running pump continues to supply the header.

beyond: Not for the exam. Multi-stage centrifugal pumps are common in boiler feed and reverse-osmosis desalination, where many stages sit in series on one shaft. City water networks switch parallel pumps in and out as demand changes, often with variable-frequency drives. Search next for pump parallel operation stability, minimum starting speed of centrifugal pump and pump curve intersection with a system curve.
